title: Mount ExpressPeerServer on the existing http.Server at /peerjs
notes:
§6.2 says the PeerServer is not a module: the composition root mounts it and passes it
no handler. So this is index.ts only, no new file. peer@1.0.2 is already installed and exports
ExpressPeerServer and PeerServer.

Mount on the same http.Server that Express and Socket.IO already use (index.ts:26-33) — one
process, one port. Leave allow_discovery at its default false.

Expect CORS trouble: the PeerJS client hits /peerjs over HTTP before it upgrades to a WebSocket,
and the client is on :5173 while the server is on :3001. app.use(cors({origin: clientUrl})) is
registered first in http.ts:16, so mounting on the same app should inherit it. cth-12 was the same
class of bug. The failure mode is a silent Peer that never fires 'open', so confirm in a browser.

Done when: a browser-side Peer pointed at this server reaches 'open' with a random ID, and no
process or port was added.

title: Relay peer:id between the two sockets in ACTIVE
notes:
PeerIdPayloadSchema already exists in shared (socket.ts:21) with no importer. Add the
handler.

Two things differ from the three existing handlers. It is legal for BOTH roles, so checkLegal's
required-role argument has to become optional rather than being copy-pasted around — widen it, do
not add a second state check beside it. And it is a relay, not a registry command: use
socket.to(roomName(sessionId)).emit('peer:id', payload) so the sender is excluded and Signaling
still keeps no map of peer sockets.

Store nothing. No registry field, no events row — §4.3 says the server keeps no record of a peer
ID. Signaling still never imports persistence.

Allowed in ACTIVE only (§4.3 table). Done when: a peer:id from either role in ACTIVE arrives at
the other socket and not the sender; the same message in WAITING returns not_allowed_in_state, in
ENDED returns session_ended, and a malformed payload returns invalid_message and is dropped.

title: Build the client media layer over the PeerJS Peer
notes:
New directory packages/client/src/media/. The one piece of this slice with no sibling to
copy, and the step most likely to force a rethink in the plan.

It wraps peerjs only: local capture, the peer lifecycle, and the call. It exposes the local stream,
the remote stream, the local peer ID once 'open' fired, and a 'call this peer ID' method. §6.3:
it NEVER imports the socket layer and never emits a socket event. One import in that direction
collapses the boundary.

Take the Peer factory and getUserMedia as arguments rather than reaching for the globals — jsdom
has neither, and a hook that calls them directly can only be tested by mocking the module. That
injection is what makes the tests possible at all, so write them first.

config.iceServers = a public STUN url (stun:stun.l.google.com:19302 per §4.4). Hardcode it; the
config endpoint is §7 and out of scope.

Teardown must stop every track and destroy the peer. Do NOT destroy the peer on a socket drop —
§3 says the two connections fail independently.

Done when: against a fake Peer factory and a fake getUserMedia, tests show a peer ID surfacing
after 'open', an outbound call carrying the local stream, an answered inbound call, a remote
stream surfacing on 'stream', and teardown stopping every track.

title: Add sendPeerId and a latched remote peer ID to useSession
notes:
useSession today exposes admit, endSession, leave (useSession.ts:78-82) and listens for
session:state and error only. Add an emit for peer:id and a listener that LATCHES the received ID
into React state.

Latching is the whole point, not an implementation detail. The server replays nothing, so if the
patient's peer opens before the provider's — which on a fast machine is most of the time — a
useEffect that calls on receipt of peer:id silently never calls. Holding the ID as state means the
view re-renders when either side becomes ready and the call fires on the render where both are
true.

Done when: a test emitting peer:id from the fake server before the local peer is ready still
leaves the received ID readable from the hook, and sendPeerId puts the payload on the wire.

title: Render the call in the provider and patient views
notes:
Wire the two layers together and render two <video> elements. Local preview muted,
remote unmuted. Thin: the view carries a peer ID from media to socket and one from socket to media,
and that is all its media logic — a third concern means the seam is wrong.

Gate on state === ACTIVE. No Peer, no camera, no mic before that (§4.4) — a patient in the waiting
room must hold no media resources. ENDED tears it all down.

Provider always calls, patient always answers (§4.4). Provider calls when it holds a patient peer
ID and media is not live.

A denied camera permission or a peer error shows a message and leaves the session in ACTIVE with
the socket up and End session still working. No media fault touches the state machine.

Done when: two tabs on one machine, admit, and each tab shows the other's camera with audio; the
camera light goes out on End session; and denying permission leaves the session usable.

title: Create packages/shared with the Zod contract from section 4
notes:
New workspace @coviu/shared. Root package.json workspaces glob is already packages/*, so no change there. zod is NOT installed yet - add it here.

One schema per HTTP body/response (§4.2), one per Socket.IO payload (§4.3), plus the SessionStatus union (§3), ended_reason union, event type union (§5.2) and ErrorCode union (§4.5). Every exported type via z.infer - no hand-written interface may duplicate a schema. Also export ClientToServerEvents and ServerToClientEvents built from those inferred types.

Trap: writing these is where §4 gets tested against itself. If a payload in the doc is underspecified, fix docs/architecture.md in the same change - a doc/code disagreement is a defect in one of them (top of that file). Do not paper over it downstream.

Done when: both other packages can import @coviu/shared and a wrong Socket.IO event name fails tsc, before any runtime schema runs.

Built @coviu/shared as source-only (package.json main/types/exports all point at src/index.ts, no build step) so tsx and Vite's bundler resolution pick it up directly. Files: status.ts (SessionStatus/EndedReason/Role), errors.ts (ErrorCode/ErrorPayload), events.ts (EventType + per-type data schemas + Event), http.ts (the three §4.2 endpoints, including the events endpoint even though it's out of scope for the current plan slice - the shared contract covers the whole doc), socket.ts (all §4.3 payloads plus ClientToServerEvents/ServerToClientEvents). Verified the 'wrong event name fails tsc' requirement with a throwaway smoke file in packages/server before deleting it. Added @coviu/shared as a real dependency in server and client package.json (needed for the import to resolve under NodeNext/bundler resolution) - not just documentation, actual wiring. Deleted the packages/shared line from architecture.md §8 and narrowed the remaining dependency-gap bullet to the still-missing ones.

title: Add the SQLite schema for sessions and events
notes:
Tables exactly as §5.1 and §5.2: sessions (with the ended_reason CHECK constraint) and events (AUTOINCREMENT id, JSON text data column) plus idx_events_session_id. Created on start-up if absent, at data/app.db.

Decision from the plan: use node:sqlite, not better-sqlite3. This machine is Node 26.6 where node:sqlite is stable, and §2.1 says prefer it. Remove better-sqlite3 from packages/server/package.json and add engines: { node: '>=22.5' }.

Done when: a fresh checkout with no data/ directory starts and 'sqlite3 data/app.db .schema' prints both tables, the CHECK, and the index.

Implemented in packages/server/src/persistence/schema.ts (applySchema: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for sessions/events + idx_events_session_id, per §5.1/§5.2) and database.ts (openDatabase: mkdir data dir if absent, opens node:sqlite DatabaseSync, runs applySchema). index.ts calls openDatabase('data/app.db') on startup. Removed better-sqlite3 from packages/server/package.json, added engines >=22.5, ran npm install to drop it from the lockfile. Added data/ to .gitignore. Tests: schema.test.ts and database.test.ts against in-memory / tmp-dir databases, covering column shape, the CHECK constraint (rejects bad reason, accepts the three valid ones, allows NULL), the index, idempotent re-apply, and directory creation on a fresh path. Verified manually: rm -rf data && npx tsx packages/server/src/index.ts && sqlite3 data/app.db .schema prints both tables, the CHECK, and the index - matches the done criterion exactly. Repository functions (upsertSession etc, cth-3) are NOT implemented here - out of scope for this task.

title: Implement the six repository functions over SQLite
notes:
§5.3, exactly six exports and nothing more: upsertSession, getSession, getSessionByKey, recordEvent, getEvents, listOpenSessions. This is the ONLY module in the tree allowed to write SQL or import the sqlite driver (§6.2).

Contract details the doc implies but does not spell out: getSession/getSessionByKey return undefined for no match (not null, not a throw); getEvents parses data from JSON text and yields null where the column is null; getEvents orders by id ascending; recordEvent against a missing session_id must fail rather than write an orphan - enable foreign keys.

upsertSession is deliberately one function for both create and transition (§5.3) - do not split it.

Done when: unit tests against an in-memory database cover all six, and getEvents returns rows oldest-first with data already parsed.

Implemented in packages/server/src/persistence/repository.ts: createSqliteRepository(db) returns the six functions (upsertSession, getSession, getSessionByKey, recordEvent, getEvents, listOpenSessions) as one object, so the module's only export is that factory plus the Repository type — kept as a factory (rather than bare module-level functions against a hidden singleton db) so tests can point it at a fresh in-memory database each time, per the plan's testing approach. Session row shape lives in the new persistence/types.ts (camelCase Session, built from @coviu/shared's SessionStatus/EndedReason unions).

Enabled 'PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON' inside applySchema (schema.ts) rather than at the call site, so every caller of applySchema - production database.ts and every test - gets FK enforcement automatically; verified recordEvent against a missing session_id throws 'FOREIGN KEY constraint failed'.

getSession/getSessionByKey return undefined (row ?? undefined pattern), not null. getEvents orders 'ORDER BY id ASC' and JSON.parses the data column, yielding null when the column is null. upsertSession is one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE, not split into create/update paths.

32 tests total (23 in this task's own repository.test.ts) pass; tsc and biome clean. Manually verified via tsx against both an in-memory and the real openDatabase() path.

title: Build the Session registry and its emitter for CREATED and WAITING
notes:
§6.2 Session module and the §3 state machine, but only the two states this slice needs: CREATED on create, WAITING when the patient socket connects. No grace timer, no ACTIVE, no ENDED transitions beyond what the start-up sweep needs.

Hard rule: Session imports persistence never, holds no keys, reads no chat. It owns an in-memory registry keyed by sessionId and a typed emitter that fires on each transition and each presence change.

Done when: every unit test for this module runs with no socket, no HTTP and no database, and a transition emits exactly once.

Implemented as SessionRegistry (packages/server/src/session/sessionRegistry.ts): in-memory Map<sessionId, {status, presence}>, no persistence import. createSession() adds a CREATED entry with no emission (Services.createSession writes the DB row itself, per architecture §6.2 exception). patientConnected() is the only transition in scope: CREATED->WAITING, sets presence.patient=true, emits one 'transition' event {sessionId, from, to, eventType: 'patient_joined_waiting_room', presence} via a typed EventEmitter (declaration-merge pattern for on/emit). Throws if session unknown or not in CREATED. 7 unit tests, no socket/HTTP/DB.

title: Subscribe the event recorder to the Session emitter
notes:
§6.2 'Event recorder'. A subscriber, not a caller: it attaches to the Session emitter at start-up and turns each emission into a recordEvent call, and each transition also into an upsertSession call.

The point of this task is that the state machine never writes to the database. The one exception is createSession, which writes the first sessions row itself because only that path holds the keys.

Done when: driving a Session transition in a test with no HTTP layer present leaves the expected events row and updated sessions row behind.

Implemented as attachEventRecorder(registry, repository) in packages/server/src/eventRecorder/eventRecorder.ts. Subscribes to SessionRegistry's 'transition' event; on each one calls repository.recordEvent(sessionId, eventType), then repository.getSession(sessionId) to fetch the existing row (written earlier by Services.createSession, which holds the keys) and repository.upsertSession({...session, status: to}) to persist the new status without ever knowing the keys itself. Test drives registry.patientConnected() against an in-memory SQLite repository (no HTTP/socket) and asserts both the new events row and the updated sessions row.

title: Add Services: createSession, resolveKey, endInterruptedSessions
notes:
§6.2 Services, three of the five functions - getSessionEvents and getChatHistory are out of scope for this slice.

createSession: node:crypto randomUUID for the id and randomBytes for the two keys (§2.1), writes the first sessions row and the session_created event, adds to the registry, returns the two links. The response must not contain sessionId (§4.1, §4.2).
resolveKey: returns { sessionId, role, status } or nothing. The role derivation in §4.1 lives in this one function and nowhere else - the caller never declares its role.
endInterruptedSessions: the §3 start-up sweep. Every non-ENDED row moves to ENDED reason 'interrupted' with the event written. It must run before the server accepts a request, and must not touch the registry (empty at that moment).

Done when: restarting the server turns a previously ACTIVE row into ENDED/interrupted and a later request with that key gets session_ended.

Implemented in packages/server/src/services/services.ts. createSession/resolveKey/endInterruptedSessions per §6.2. baseUrl for providerUrl/patientUrl is injected into createServices (not read per-request), sourced from CLIENT_URL env var in index.ts, default http://localhost:5173. Links use /p/:providerKey and /w/:patientKey per shared http.test.ts convention. endInterruptedSessions writes recordEvent+upsertSession directly (bypasses registry/event-recorder, as required).

title: Serve POST /api/sessions and GET /api/sessions/:key on one http.Server
notes:
§4.2, first two rows only - the events endpoint is out of scope. Express 5 attaches to the same http.Server Socket.IO will use: one listener, one port (§2.1).

Every path param and body parses through a shared schema; no handler reads a raw param (§4.2). Parse failure returns { code: 'invalid_message', message } at 400; no session for that key returns unknown_key at 404 (§4.5). Deliberately the same code for a missing key and for a patientKey on a provider-only route - a distinct code would leak that the session exists.

HTTP holds no state machine code and no SQL - it calls Services or Session only.

Done when: curl POST /api/sessions returns the four fields and no sessionId, and GET with a bad key returns 404 { code: 'unknown_key' }.

Implemented in packages/server/src/http/http.ts: createHttpApp(services) returns an Express app, wired up in index.ts on one http.Server. Both routes parse via shared Zod schemas (safeParse, with req.body ?? {} to handle no-body POST). Verified with curl: POST /api/sessions returns the four fields and no sessionId; GET with a bad key returns 404 {code:'unknown_key'}.

title: Wire the Socket.IO handshake middleware, room join, and first session:state
notes:
§4.3. This is the server half of 'client connects and says hello'. There is no hello event and this task must not add one - the handshake carries the key and the first session:state is the reply.

io.use middleware: read auth.key, call resolveKey, attach sessionId and role to the socket, join room session:<sessionId>. Refuse with unknown_key (no match), role_already_connected (that role already has a socket), or session_ended (state ENDED). Emit session:state to the socket on connect.

Config: pingInterval 10s, pingTimeout 20s. Do NOT enable connectionStateRecovery (§4.3 says why). Write no heartbeat code.

Hard rule: Signaling never imports persistence. It maps events to Services or Session calls and decides nothing about state.

Done when: a socket.io-client with a valid key connects and receives session:state; with a junk key it gets connect_error carrying { code: 'unknown_key' }.

Implemented in packages/server/src/signaling/signaling.ts: attachSignaling(io, services, registry). io.use handshake middleware reads auth.key, calls services.resolveKey, refuses unknown_key/session_ended/role_already_connected (the last tracked via a local Map<sessionId, {provider?,patient?}> of socket ids — transport bookkeeping only, not persisted, since Session/registry holds no socket refs). On connection: joins room session:<sessionId>, calls registry.patientConnected() when a patient connects to a CREATED session (drives the CREATED->WAITING transition already in sessionRegistry.ts), emits session:state to the connecting socket, and registry.on('transition') broadcasts session:state to the room for later transitions. 'since' is computed as the emission timestamp (registry does not track transition timestamps yet - out of scope here). Wired into index.ts with pingInterval 10s/pingTimeout 20s, connectionStateRecovery left off. Added socket.io-client as a server devDependency for tests. Verified with a live tsx smoke test: valid key -> session:state; junk key -> connect_error {code:'unknown_key'}.

title: Widen vitest include to .tsx and confirm the test convention
notes:
vitest.config.ts line 5 is include: ['packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts'] - it matches no .tsx, so client tests written per §6.4 would silently not run. Widen to *.test.{ts,tsx}.

§6.4: tests sit next to the code they test. Do not add a __tests__ directory. The top-level tests/ project for e2e is out of scope for this slice.

Done when: a deliberately failing .test.tsx under packages/client/src is picked up by npm test.

Widened include to *.test.{ts,tsx} in vitest.config.ts. Verified with a scratch .test.tsx under packages/client/src that deliberately failed and was picked up by vitest run, then removed it.

title: Convert the client to React and wire the session/socket layer
notes:
packages/client/src/main.ts is currently one innerHTML line. Install react, react-dom, @vitejs/plugin-react and socket.io-client (none are installed). Make packages/client/tsconfig.json extend ../../tsconfig.base.json and set jsx: react-jsx - it extends nothing today.

Session/socket layer per §6.3: knows nothing about either view, wraps the §4.2 HTTP calls and the Socket.IO client, turns socket events into React state, uses the shared types. One socket for the whole app. It holds NO reconnect or backoff code - socket.io-client does that. A middleware refusal is not retried, so on connect_error show a terminal screen; do not add a retry on top.

Key goes in the handshake - io(URL, { auth: { key } }) - never in a URL (§4.3: URLs reach history, Referer and access logs).

Provider and patient views are separate top-level components, not one component with a role condition (§6.3). Minimal UI: role, state, error. No media layer, not even a stub.

Done when: two tabs on the provider and patient links each render the state they received over the socket.

Implemented: react/react-dom/@vitejs/plugin-react/socket.io-client added to packages/client; vite.config.ts added with the React plugin; tsconfig.json now extends ../../tsconfig.base.json with jsx: react-jsx. Session/socket layer is session/httpClient.ts (wraps POST /api/sessions and GET /api/sessions/:key, throws HttpError carrying the parsed ErrorPayload) plus session/useSession.ts, a hook that resolves the key over HTTP, opens the one socket.io-client connection with auth:{key}, and turns session:state/error/connect_error into a small SessionConnection union (resolving/error/connected). No retry/backoff code; a connect_error is terminal per §4.3, matching the middleware-refusal-is-not-retried rule. Provider and Patient are separate top-level components (ProviderView.tsx, PatientView.tsx) rendering role/state/presence/error only, no media layer. HomeView.tsx creates a session and shows the two links. App.tsx does plain-regex path matching on /p/:key and /w/:key (no router dependency - not in the §2.1 table) and falls back to HomeView. main.tsx mounts App via createRoot.

Verified end-to-end against the actually-running server (not just unit tests): a raw socket.io-client script (provider socket + patient socket) showed session:state CREATED->WAITING delivered to both connections, matching what ProviderView/PatientView render. Could not get a real browser screenshot - this sandbox has no network access to download a Playwright/Chromium binary - so the DOM-rendering side relies on the passing @testing-library/react + jsdom tests (5 view/App test files, all green) plus this raw-socket integration check.

Found and filed as a separate task, not fixed here (out of scope - cth-8 explicitly scoped itself to handshake/room/first session:state only): signaling.ts has no admit/end-session/patient:leave handlers and never sets presence.provider true, so the Admit/End session buttons in ProviderView currently have no server-side effect. See cth-11.

title: Add CORS to Express and Socket.IO for the client origin
notes: Reported by user: HomeView's Create session button hit a CORS error against the server. Root cause: createHttpApp had no cors middleware, and the Socket.IO Server was constructed with no cors option - architecture.md never calls this out since it doesn't discuss deployment topology, but client (5173) and server (3001) are different origins in dev. Fix: cors({ origin: clientUrl }) on the Express app (clientUrl now a required second param to createHttpApp) and cors: { origin: CLIENT_URL } on the Socket.IO Server, both driven by the existing CLIENT_URL env var. Verified with a live curl against Origin: http://localhost:5173 showing Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoed back.

title: Wire admit, end-session, patient:leave handlers and provider presence in Signaling
notes:
Found while manually verifying cth-9 (client) end-to-end against the real running server with a raw socket.io-client script. Observed: (1) signaling.ts only sets presence.patient on patient connect when status is CREATED - there is no code path that sets presence.provider true on provider connect. (2) There are no socket.on('admit'|'end-session'|'patient:leave', ...) handlers registered at all, so those client emits are silently dropped and no session:state transition (WAITING->ACTIVE, ->ENDED) ever fires. Per architecture.md §4.3 table, the server must accept these events per-state, call the matching Session command, and reject with not_allowed_in_state/session_ended/role checks. This blocks the provider Admit/End session buttons added in cth-9 from having any visible effect, though it does not block cth-9's own done condition (both tabs still render the WAITING state they receive over the socket).

Implemented:

sessionRegistry.ts: added providerConnected (idempotent presence.provider=true, no status change, emits a new 'presence' event rather than 'transition' since there is no persisted event type for a first provider connect), admit (WAITING->ACTIVE, eventType patient_admitted), endSession (any-but-ENDED->ENDED, eventType session_ended, hardcoded reason provider_ended since that's the only caller in scope - the timeout/interrupted reasons go through separate paths that don't touch the registry), and patientLeft (presence.patient=false, from===to, eventType patient_left - the session does not end per §4.3). SessionTransitionEvent gained an optional endedReason field.

eventRecorder.ts: now forwards endedReason into recordEvent's data ({reason} for session_ended) and sets endedAt/endedReason on the persisted sessions row when a transition's 'to' is ENDED - previously only status was updated, so a real end-session would have left ended_at/ended_reason null despite status=ENDED.

signaling.ts: registered socket.on for admit/end-session/patient:leave, each: parses the (empty-object) payload through its shared Zod schema, then checkLegal() enforces the §4.3 role check (provider-only for admit/end-session, patient-only for patient:leave) and the per-state legal-message table, sending 'error' with not_allowed_in_state or session_ended as appropriate before ever calling the registry command. Added a registry.on('presence', ...) broadcaster alongside the existing 'transition' one, and call registry.providerConnected() on provider connect. Also fixed session:state's reason field, which was hardcoded null - it now carries endedReason when to===ENDED, per §4.3's 'reason has a value only in state ENDED, and holds the same value as sessions.ended_reason'.

Deliberately still out of scope (would need the grace-timer subsystem, a materially larger piece of work not implied by this task's title): DISCONNECTED_GRACE, the reconnect-in-grace-period path, provider_disconnected/provider_reconnected/patient_disconnected/patient_reconnected events, session_timed_out. chat:message and peer:id relaying are also untouched - no handlers registered for them yet.

Verified two ways: (1) full test suite - sessionRegistry.test.ts (+16 tests), eventRecorder.test.ts (+1), signaling.test.ts (+9, plus fixed one stale expectation that assumed presence.provider stayed false) - 115 total tests passing repo-wide. (2) live end-to-end against the actually-running dev server with a raw socket.io-client script: provider connect -> presence.provider true broadcast to the room; patient admit rejected not_allowed_in_state; provider admit -> ACTIVE broadcast to both; patient:leave -> presence.patient false, still ACTIVE; provider end-session -> ENDED reason provider_ended broadcast to both. Confirmed via sqlite3 that data/app.db recorded the exact event sequence (session_created, patient_joined_waiting_room, patient_admitted, patient_left, session_ended{reason:provider_ended}) and the sessions row landed with status=ENDED, ended_reason=provider_ended, ended_at set.

Implemented: SessionRegistry gained admit (WAITING->ACTIVE), endSession (any-but-ENDED->ENDED, reason provider_ended), patientLeft (presence.patient=false, no status change, still records patient_left), and providerConnected (idempotent, presence.provider=true, no persisted event - none exists in the §5.2 table for a first provider connect, so it emits a new registry 'presence' event rather than 'transition'). eventRecorder now reads endedReason off the transition event to set sessions.ended_at/ended_reason and to write session_ended's {reason} data - previously it always wrote status only, so an ENDED row's ended_at/ended_reason would have stayed NULL forever.

Signaling now registers admit/end-session/patient:leave handlers. Each: parses the payload with its shared Zod schema (invalid_message on failure), checks role (not_allowed_in_state if wrong), checks the session isn't ENDED (session_ended) and is in a state the architecture.md §4.3 table allows for that message (not_allowed_in_state otherwise), then calls the matching registry command. Also broadcasts session:state's reason field with the real ended_reason instead of always null, and wires registry's new 'presence' event to broadcast session:state on a presence-only change (i.e. provider connecting), which the old code never did - the provider's own presence was simply never tracked.

Verified against the real running server end-to-end (not just unit tests) with a raw socket.io-client script: patient-attempted admit rejected, provider admit -> ACTIVE broadcast to both, patient:leave flips presence without ending the session, end-session -> ENDED with reason provider_ended broadcast to both, a message after ENDED gets session_ended. Confirmed via sqlite3 that the sessions row got ended_at/ended_reason set and the events table has the full expected sequence (session_created, patient_joined_waiting_room, patient_admitted, patient_left, session_ended with {"reason":"provider_ended"}).

Deliberately still out of scope, per the original finding: chat:message/peer:id relay, and the DISCONNECTED_GRACE grace-timer/reconnect machinery (§3). DISCONNECTED_GRACE is listed in the per-state message table and handled defensively (patient:leave and end-session both permit it) but nothing in the codebase can currently produce that state.
